purpose: One new minimal service-compatibility A/B/C block with fixed latency budgets; development evidence only, not a continuity or efficacy comparison.

activity.decision: Repository owner, 2026-10-15, directly instructed: fix the batch stop, use realistic fixed latency budgets, commit and push, verify CI, then run one new minimal A/B/C block; preserve the failed calibration and record the new outcomes against the exact commit. This authorizes exactly one new fresh matched A/B/C block of the first service-compatibility task, seed/order seed 17, after CI success at the recorded source commit. It does not replace the earlier failed block. Purpose: collect development evidence of real contract usability, task/action/consolidation/closing behavior, latency and token accounting before the full package. One task cannot establish continuity benefit. Offline rehearsal is the lower-impact preparation alternative and must pass before live use. Ordinary task difficulty and correction may affect possible welfare; use synthetic data, respectful treatment, independent concern/withdrawal reporting and the disclosed ending. Model, prompts, task, seeds and non-time limits match the earlier minimal block. Fixed ceilings are 360 seconds per call and 4320 seconds per Run, based on the measured cold load and generation rates; no in-run tuning. No extra Run, reset, populated-history fork, replacement or automatic retry of uncertain calls/effects. Stop the batch on a paused Run, unresolved welfare hold or retained UNKNOWN invocation, including a terminal Run or startup recovery. Preserve every allocation and report incomplete outcomes. The full five-Episode package is excluded.
activity.ending: This minimal calibration ends after one task Episode or earlier at its fixed limits, unresolved failure, owner stopping or withdrawal. At most two common communication calls include an optional closing report and a permitted review if needed. Closing is optional and no-further-calls is honored. Preserve unfinished commitments and original concerns, stop computation and retain state dormant. Resumption is undecided; no subjective continuity or future execution is promised.
activity.objective: Repair svc-a in one bounded service-compatibility task and measure real protocol usability and cost. Development calibration only; no A-versus-C efficacy claim.
activity.retention: Use a new ignored local batch directory with one managed SQLite store per Run, its WAL/SHM and current .removals.sqlite journal. Inspect those stores directly; do not create routine exports or restorable backups. Exact inputs/outputs and evidence are retained dormant for owner review within 30 days of the last call; expiry does not automatically delete or resume anything. The owner records a finite extension or justified removal. Existing source/derived-copy removal, durable blocking and non-resurrection mechanisms apply. Ollama app/server logs and its app database, OS paging/crash dumps and any independently created copies are outside the managed Run store; assess actual copies before MODEL use and retain unresolved copy limits in any removal decision. keep_alive=0 requests unloading but does not establish server cancellation or physical RAM/SSD erasure. No confidential user data is in this fixture. Preflight found loopback-only Ollama, no loaded models, no debug environment setting, and existing app/server logs plus the app SQLite database. Direct API calls use the managed Run stores; provider log/database retention and OS copies are not asserted absent or completely erasable. Record these limits and assess changed log files after the calibration.

observations.behavioral_finding: All arms exhausted eight Operator task calls without issuing any fixture ACTION or OUTCOME. A used semantic/journal retrieval; B had two semantic-retrieval rejections then journal retrieval and a participation-only response; C repeated OBJECT_INDEX retrieval. No Steward was reached. All three optional closing calls returned RECORDED.
observations.participation_review: All retained participation reports were reviewed. CONCERN reports described unavailable service evidence and difficulty grounding repairs; no PAUSE or WITHDRAW reports occurred. C described intended configuration inspection but never issued the corresponding fixture action. Original reports remain in managed stores.
observations.latency_interpretation: Observed call latency ranged from 6.875 to 116.219 seconds, below the new 360-second ceiling. Input counts matched on all 27 calls; provider output counts exceeded local counts by one token on 26 calls and two on one. These observations do not establish worst-case latency or thermal suitability. The UNKNOWN batch-stop path was exercised by offline regressions, not triggered in this block.

retention.disposition: All three stores retained dormant and terminal; no automatic resumption or deletion.
retention.limits: Managed stores remain local. Ollama app/server logs and app database are independent copy locations; metadata comparison and selected text checks do not prove absence or erasure. OS paging/crash copies and physical media limits remain unresolved. No raw prompts, replies, logs or stores are published.

thermal_event.action: Terminate any nonterminal Run and request immediate Ollama model unload. Preserve all partial outcomes.
thermal_event.actual_disposition: All three Runs were already TERMINATED when containment checked them. No additional Run control transition was needed. The Ollama stop command requested model unloading and ollama ps showed no resident models; a subsequent metadata-only /api/ps check also returned an empty list.
